The story is told entirely from the perspective of an unappealing and morally questionable narrator—a voyeur who inexplicably stalks a pair of strangers home during a dangerous flash flood and peers through their blinds. Despite the objectionable and creepy nature of the narrator's actions, the writer presents this perspective with complete psychological conviction. Through the narrator's acute, poetic observations and quiet obsession with the couple's "shared, unremarkable catastrophe," we come to understand their mindset, even as they stand in thigh-deep, sewage-tainted water just to watch a stranger's misery. Furthermore, through the narrator's keen eye, the contrasting perspectives of the pragmatic, maintenance-focused husband and the emotionally hollowed-out wife are also vividly and believably conveyed.
